name: Tirzepatide

lead: Tirzepatide is a weekly injectable sold as Mounjaro and Zepbound. People use it to cut body fat, and the face leans out as weight comes off.

It activates both GIP and GLP-1 receptors, which lowers appetite and calorie intake. In the SURMOUNT-1 trial, average weight change at 72 weeks was about -15.0, -19.5 and -20.9 percent across the three studied strengths, among the largest reductions reported for an approved anti-obesity drug. Facial leaning follows total fat loss, and with larger losses, facial volume loss and skin laxity can be more noticeable in some users.

paras: It is prescribed as a once-weekly injection, with the amount stepped up gradually by the prescriber. Users combine it with high protein intake and resistance training to preserve muscle. Results build over months, and weight returns after stopping.

Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea and constipation are common, mostly while the amount is being increased. Pancreatitis, gallbladder disease and dehydration-related kidney injury have been reported, and the label carries a thyroid C-cell tumour warning. It can reduce the effectiveness of oral contraceptives. Lean mass is lost along with fat. It is prescription-only; unregulated peptide-vial sources add contamination and accuracy risks.

angle.text: Users take tirzepatide to cut body fat, with strong appetite suppression creating a larger calorie deficit and a leaner body and face. Trials show some of the largest weight losses of any approved drug; facial leanness and muscle retention are discussed mainly by users.

lead: Tirzepatide is an injectable peptide that activates both the glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) receptor and the glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor. Made by Eli Lilly, it is given once weekly and sold as Mounjaro for type 2 diabetes and as Zepbound for chronic weight management and, in the United States, moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea [1][2].

In the SURMOUNT-1 phase 3 trial of adults with obesity or overweight without diabetes, mean weight change at 72 weeks was about -15.0, -19.5 and -20.9 percent at the 5, 10 and 15 mg weekly doses, against about -3.1 percent on placebo [1][3]. A DXA substudy found that about three quarters of the weight lost was fat mass and about a quarter lean mass [4]. These are among the largest average reductions reported for an approved anti-obesity drug, and in a 2025 head-to-head trial it was compared directly with semaglutide [5].

People who pursue looks improvement discuss tirzepatide as a systemic fat-loss tool: by reducing appetite it lowers body fat, which in turn changes how the jawline, cheeks and midsection show. Facial leaning follows overall fat loss rather than being targeted. Its documented adverse effects are mostly gastrointestinal, and the US label carries a boxed warning on thyroid C-cell tumors observed in rodents [2]. Weight regain after stopping is documented, and forum users also discuss unregulated peptide supplies, whose contents regulators say have not been verified [6].
infobox: -15.0 to -20.9 percent at 72 weeks, versus -3.1 percent on placebo [1]

paras: Mounjaro is indicated as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes, and the US label extends this to pediatric patients aged 10 and above [2]. Zepbound is indicated alongside a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity for long-term weight reduction in adults with obesity, or overweight with at least one weight-related condition, and for moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea in adults with obesity [1]. The FDA approved the sleep apnea indication in December 2024 [1].

Appearance-focused users take tirzepatide to lose body fat through appetite reduction. It has no known mechanism for removing facial fat selectively; changes to the face are described as following total fat loss, and forum members who report on the drug describe strong hunger suppression [7][8]. The larger average weight loss compared with older drugs means that facial volume loss may be more noticeable in some people, according to forum discussion, although no trial has studied facial appearance.

SURMOUNT-1 randomized 2,539 adults with a BMI of 30 or higher, or 27 or higher with a weight-related complication and no diabetes, to weekly tirzepatide or placebo for 72 weeks [3]. A three-year follow-up reported safety outcomes and effects on progression to type 2 diabetes in people with obesity and prediabetes [9]. In people with type 2 diabetes and obesity, SURMOUNT-2 tested the drug against placebo [10].

In the SURPASS-2 trial in type 2 diabetes, tirzepatide at 5, 10 and 15 mg was compared with semaglutide over 40 weeks [11], and network meta-analyses have compared tirzepatide with semaglutide and other GLP-1 drugs on blood glucose and body weight [12][13]. A 2025 head-to-head trial in obesity without diabetes compared the maximum tolerated doses of the two drugs in an open-label design [5].

Body composition has been reported in a SURMOUNT-1 substudy [4]. A 2025 network meta-analysis of 22 randomized trials found that GLP-1 receptor agonists and dual agonists reduced fat mass and lean mass, with lean mass about a quarter of the total loss across the class [14].

Maintenance and discontinuation have been studied. SURMOUNT-4 randomized participants who had lost weight on tirzepatide either to continue or to switch to placebo [15]. Wikipedia reports that participants regained on average about 53 percent of their lost weight within a year of stopping, and a 2025 meta-analysis of GLP-1 drugs examined weight after discontinuation [1][16].

sections.h: Effects on body composition and appearance
paras: For appearance-focused users the interest lies in fat loss. A DXA substudy of 160 SURMOUNT-1 participants reported that over 72 weeks tirzepatide reduced body weight by about 21 percent, fat mass by about 34 percent and lean mass by about 11 percent, with roughly 75 percent of the weight lost being fat [4]. A 2025 network meta-analysis of GLP-1 receptor agonists and co-agonists likewise found reductions in both fat and lean mass, with lean mass making up about a quarter of the loss [14].

Because the loss is systemic, the face thins along with the body. Reviews of GLP-1 receptor agonists discuss facial fat reduction and skin laxity after rapid weight loss, a pattern popularly called "Ozempic face" [17]. People who value a leaner, more angular face describe this as part of the appeal; others describe wanting to keep facial volume and look to fillers or gradual loss. Resistance training and protein intake are commonly discussed in these circles as ways to preserve lean mass during a cut, an idea that appears in forum logs rather than in the tirzepatide trials [18][19].

The most common adverse effects are nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, decreased appetite, constipation and abdominal discomfort or pain, which mostly occur during dose escalation and increase with dose [1]. In the 2018 phase 2 diabetes trial summarized by Wikipedia, 25 percent of participants on the 15 mg dose discontinued compared with 5.1 percent on 5 mg [1].

The US label carries a boxed warning for thyroid C-cell tumors in rodents and contraindicates the drug in people with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 [2]. Other labelled warnings include acute pancreatitis, hypoglycemia with insulin or insulin secretagogues, hypersensitivity reactions, acute kidney injury from volume depletion and severe gastrointestinal reactions [2]. The label says pregnancy data are insufficient and animal studies show possible fetal risk [2]. A pharmacovigilance analysis of reports to the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System has also examined tirzepatide signals [20]. A large meta-analysis of GLP-1 receptor agonist trials assessed mortality, cardiovascular events and serious adverse events across the class [21].

Wikipedia reports that a 2024 systematic review found no association with pancreatitis, though later case reports exist, and that in January 2026 the UK MHRA warned of a small risk of severe acute pancreatitis. It also reports that in January 2026 the FDA requested removal of the suicidal behavior and ideation warning from GLP-1 receptor agonist labels, citing studies since 2024 that do not support a link [1]. Rapid weight loss also brings loss of lean mass and facial volume, covered above [4][17].

Tirzepatide selectively activates the GIP and GLP-1 receptors. It is more potent than native GIP at the GIP receptor, while at the GLP-1 receptor it shows bias toward cAMP signaling over beta-arrestin recruitment [1][2]. GLP-1 activity reduces appetite and slows gastric emptying; the added role of GIP agonism is under study. The label states that tirzepatide enhances first- and second-phase insulin secretion and reduces glucagon in a glucose-dependent manner [2]. Wikipedia reports increases in adiponectin of up to 26 percent after 26 weeks at 10 mg [1]. A 2026 meta-analysis reported reductions in inflammatory markers hsCRP and IL-6 versus placebo [22].

Tirzepatide is a modified analog of human GIP with a C20 fatty diacid attached via a linker to a lysine side chain; the fatty acid binds albumin and prolongs half-life to about five days, allowing weekly dosing [1][23][2].

Eli Lilly filed patents on tirzepatide synthesis and on its use for glycemic control in 2016 [1]. A 2018 phase 2 trial in The Lancet reported that nausea, vomiting and diarrhea rose with dose, with discontinuation of about 25 percent at the 15 mg dose against 5.1 percent at the 5 mg dose [1]. Phase 3 trials were completed globally by 2021, including SURPASS-2 against semaglutide, and Lilly applied for FDA approval with a priority review voucher [1][11].

The FDA approved Mounjaro for type 2 diabetes in May 2022, the European Union followed in September 2022, Canada in November 2022 and Australia in December 2022 [1]. Lilly announced in April 2022 that phase 3 results in people with overweight or obesity without diabetes met their endpoints, and SURMOUNT-1 was published that year [1][3]. Zepbound was approved for weight management in November 2023, the same month the UK regulator extended Mounjaro to weight management, and in December 2024 it became the first medicine approved for moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea in adults with obesity [1][24].

In August 2024 the three-year SURMOUNT-1 results reported a lower risk of progression to type 2 diabetes in people with prediabetes, and a trial in obesity with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction reported fewer major cardiovascular events than placebo [1][9][25]. A 72-week open-label trial in 2025 reported greater weight loss with tirzepatide than with semaglutide [5]. Lilly's next-generation drug retatrutide, which also acts on the glucagon receptor, reported phase 3 TRIUMPH results in 2026 [26].

Bodybuilding and appearance forums discuss tirzepatide alongside testosterone therapy, other peptides and dieting. T Nation members describe using or planning to use it for cutting and to curb appetite, and one clinic owner lists weight-loss injections as part of a service mix [19][27][18][28]. A looksmax.org post in a long personal guide covers tirzepatide in a section on fat loss [29]. Some posters compare it with retatrutide, saying the latter is better for fat loss and tirzepatide for hunger control [7][30]. Members also mention insurance not covering the drugs and the existence of compounded supply [27].

Wikipedia reports counterfeit Ozempic pens in Europe in 2023 that possibly contained insulin and led to hospitalisations, and an FDA warning on counterfeit semaglutide in December 2023 [31]. Looksmaxxing coverage notes that some people without medical conditions obtain GLP-1 drugs through unregulated channels [32].

The FDA declared a tirzepatide shortage in December 2022 and declared it resolved in October 2024, with enforcement against compounders delayed to the end of 2024 after a lawsuit by compounding pharmacies [1]. The FDA states that compounded and unapproved versions are not reviewed for safety, effectiveness or quality, and as of May 2026 had received more than 730 adverse event reports associated with compounded tirzepatide, while noting underreporting and that causation is not always clear [6].

The agency has warned about products labelled "for research purposes" or "not for human consumption" that were sold for human use, about fraudulent labels naming pharmacies that did not make the product, and about dosing errors with compounded injectables [6]. The National Association of Boards of Pharmacy says tens of thousands of online pharmacies operate out of compliance [1]. The same FDA page says retatrutide cannot be used in compounding under federal law and that warnings have been sent to companies involved [6]. Wikipedia reports lawsuits by Lilly against sellers of grey-market retatrutide in 2026 [26].

Tirzepatide prescriptions exceeded 6 million in the US in 2023 [1]. Wikipedia reports shifting US coverage policy for weight-loss use of GLP-1 drugs in 2025 and 2026, including announced lower cash prices for Medicare-covered people and a temporary Medicare bridge program [1]. Forum members mention insurance not covering the drugs as a reason they look at compounded supply [27].

Tirzepatide has been evaluated in a large randomized trial program. For obesity, SURMOUNT-1 (with a three-year extension), SURMOUNT-2 (type 2 diabetes), SURMOUNT-4 (maintenance) and the sleep apnea trials are principal publications [3][9][10][15][24]. SURPASS trials, including SURPASS-2 against semaglutide, tested it in type 2 diabetes [11]. Other randomized trials examined heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and obesity [25] and steatohepatitis with fibrosis [33], and a 2025 trial compared it with semaglutide in obesity [5]. Registered studies are exploring further conditions, including central centrifugal cicatricial alopecia [34]. No published trial has tested tirzepatide for facial appearance.

lore.intro: Tirzepatide is discussed on bodybuilding and appearance forums as the strongest available appetite-control drug, often compared with semaglutide and retatrutide [7][30].

claims.claim: Tirzepatide is more effective for fat loss than semaglutide.
It strongly suppresses hunger, making a cut easier.
The weight loss stops showing in the mirror or damages metabolism.
Small doses of the drug are enough for lean users.
Compounded or research-peptide tirzepatide is a practical alternative to prescription supply.
The leaner face from GLP-1 weight loss is a desirable side effect.
Research-labelled or vendor-supplied tirzepatide is equivalent to the pharmacy product.
Lifting and high protein protect muscle while on the drug.

timeline.event: Eli Lilly files patents on tirzepatide synthesis and glycemic-control use [1].
Phase 2 trial in The Lancet reports dose-related gastrointestinal effects [1].
SURPASS-2 compares tirzepatide with semaglutide in type 2 diabetes [11]; Lilly applies for FDA approval [1].
Mounjaro approved in the US (May), EU (September), Canada (November) and Australia (December); SURMOUNT-1 published [1][3]. FDA declares a shortage in December [1].
Approval for obstructive sleep apnea (December); FDA declares shortage resolved (October); three-year SURMOUNT-1 results [1][9][24].
Head-to-head trial versus semaglutide in obesity published; SURMOUNT-1 DXA body composition substudy published [4][5].
